subject: Enterprise volume agreement — per-token tiers, rate protections & CPI cap
messages:
From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@calyxai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@calyxai.com, amelia.ross@calyxai.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up and pricing expectations for enterprise commit

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Calyx is finalizing requirements and procurement asked for a short written summary of your volume pricing and guidance on any protections we can expect (price locks, CPI adjustments, MFN clauses). We’ve included our estimated run-rate (see attached RFP) but the ask is: can Redwood commit to a fixed per-token rate for 12–24 months? If not, what alternative protections do you offer — e.g., CPI cap, most-favored-nation, or annual price increase ceilings?

We're also evaluating whether a commit tier approach with quarterly true-ups makes sense vs. a simple monthly usage billing model. Please include suggested commit tiers and overage mechanics.

Appreciate a concise bulletized response we can share with procurement and legal.

Best,
Jordan Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Calyx Analytics

Attachment: Calyx_RFP_20260517.pdf (pdf, 2.1MB)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@calyxai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up and pricing expectations for enterprise commit

Jordan —

Thanks for sending the RFP — good context. High level answers below, followed by proposed commit tiers and protections. Happy to set a short call to walk through.

Summary: we can offer structured commit tiers with a 12-month price lock on per-token rates for committed volumes. For customers that require longer protection we can provide a 24-month price lock with an MFN-lite clause and a capped annual CPI adjustment (we typically cap at CPI + 1.5% in long-term deals).

Proposed commit tiers (example, USD per 1K tokens):
- 0–10M tokens/month: $0.045
- 10–50M tokens/month: $0.033
- 50–200M tokens/month: $0.025
- >200M tokens/month: custom enterprise tier (apply for negotiated rate)

Overage mechanics: monthly true-up: committed tier buys a discount on expected monthly run-rate; usage above commit billed at the next tier rate with a 10% overage buffer pricing for sudden spikes during first 2 months. Annual true-up and reconciliation at contract anniversary.

Rate protections options (pick one or combine):
A) 12-month price lock on committed per-token rate (no CPI changes) — standard for committed volume contracts.
B) 24-month price lock with CPI cap: CPI increases only up to max 3% annually (absolute cap), with a step-down option if realized CPI < cap.
C) MFN-lite: Redwood will not offer a published per-token rate to any comparable customer in the same region and scale that is materially lower than Calyx’s committed rate during the lock period (carve-outs for one-off strategic partnerships).

Other notes: currency is USD; overage billing is in arrears; we can include a 30-day termination right for material breaches. I attached a draft pricing spreadsheet and SOW.

Next steps: I’ll loop in finance for final legal language. If useful, I can circulate a marked draft with explicit MFN and CPI clause language. When would procurement like a countersigned term sheet?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_draft_pricing_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB), SOW_Calyx_Redwood.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx — negotiate MFN/CPI guardrails

Team —

Reviewing Jordan's asks and Vanessa's draft. Quick negotiation playbook suggestions from finance/legal POV:
1) MFN-lite: accept but limit to 'published' list prices and exclude named strategic deals / channel partners. Also restrict MFN to same deployment mode (hosted API) and region.
2) CPI cap: prefer a formula tied to US CPI-U with a hard cap at 3%/yr for multi-year deals. Do not allow negative CPI adjustments (no credits when deflation).
3) Price lock: 12 months standard; 24 months acceptable if Calyx commits to a minimum ARR threshold (e.g., $900k ARR or 18 months of average committed spend).
4) Audit/right to request rate comparison: allow Calyx to request evidence but require narrow scope and NDA protection for any third-party rate disclosure.

I'll prepare sample contract language for MFN-lite and CPI cap. For deals that are near our top-tier volumes, we keep flexibility to offer additional credits rather than deeper per-token discounts.

Rishi
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx — negotiate MFN/CPI guardrails

Acknowledged — I like the minimum-ARR lever for 24-month locks. Two quick tactical concessions for Vanessa to propose:
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit (offsetting first month of overage) instead of deeper per-token cuts for first 3 months.
- Make MFN subject to 'comparable customer' definition (same industry vertical + within 2x run-rate).

If Calyx pushes hard on MFN, we can offer an annual rate review rather than a full MFN audit.

— Lauren
Head of Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@calyxai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Revised offering & term sheet — Calyx Analytics (summary)

Jordan —

Following internal alignment, attached is a short term sheet summarizing: 12-month price lock for committed volumes (option to extend to 24 months with an ARR threshold), MFN-lite limited to published hosted-API rates in the same region/scale, and a CPI cap clause (max 3% annual increase) for extended locks. We are also offering a $25k onboarding credit tied to the first quarter usage.

Key commercial highlights:
- Commit tiers as previously shared (see pricing sheet).
- Monthly true-ups with annual reconciliation.
- Overage charged at the next tier rate; first two months of spiky usage eligible for a 10% buffer.
- DocuSign link for the term sheet attached if you’re ready to proceed.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/REDWOOD-CALYX-ENT-2026

If procurement/legal want specific MFN wording for review, we can provide the contract excerpt. Can we get an indication of target signature date?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@calyxai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@calyxai.com>, procurement@calyxai.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised offering & term sheet — Calyx Analytics (summary)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the onboarding credit — that's helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and finance:
1) The MFN-lite carve-outs: can you provide a one-paragraph example of what would be considered a valid strategic carve-out? (procurement wants to understand when MFN doesn't apply).
2) CPI cap: procurement asks whether the 3% cap is absolute or 'up to CPI + X'. They prefer 'up to CPI + 0%' (i.e., absolute CPI only) rather than an added premium. Can Redwood consider CPI-only for the 24-month lock?
3) DocuSign: procurement will review the term sheet this week — target signature next week if legal is satisfied.

If you can send the sample MFN carve-out language and a quick note on whether CPI-only is possible for 24 months, we can share with legal.

Regards,
Jordan Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Calyx Analytics
